Benchmarks

How many tokens and how much time an agent spends on the same job, what replaying a saved Flow costs, and which web actions run in the background in Safari. Each measurement states its conditions once.

53.5% fewer input tokens on the same tasks

Codex’s built-in computer use and Haejo were given the same three tasks, each run once in a fresh conversation. The numbers cover everything from working out the steps to running them and the final reply.

Totals over 3 paired tasks · time is the mean
MeasureHaejoCodex built-in computer use
Tasks completed3/33/3
Total input tokens201,44753.5% fewer433,312
Input tokens excluding cache reads22,11956.3% fewer50,592
Output tokens1,6051,604
Mean time42.10 s8.8% shorter46.17 s

2026-10-14 · a development build of Haejo · Codex CLI 0.161.0, requested model gpt-6.1-sol, medium reasoning effort · tasks on a macOS test app we built: turn a bonus on, turn it off, and cope with a renamed button. On the bonus-off task Codex’s built-in computer use was faster (37.91 s against 48.55 s). The measurement record calls the other side Sky.

Replaying a saved Flow: zero model calls

An 11-step Flow (five inputs, a conditional checkbox, compute, review, completion check) was replayed with different values, and we deliberately changed the screen or made completion impossible to confirm.

11-step Flow · all 9 scenarios ended as expected
SituationResult
10 replays with different values10/10 completed · 0 model calls
All normal jobs13/13 completed
Two buttons changed within one jobThose steps repaired, job completed · 2 model calls
Completion could not be confirmed5/5 stopped on the spot · 0 inputs sent again

2026-10-14 · a development build of Haejo · a macOS test app we built.

20 of 22 Safari page actions run in the background

Actions were sent to a page in the person’s own Safari and judged by the events and values the page actually received. Haejo starts with the quietest route and names the route in the result.

22 kinds of page action
RouteActionsYour screen
Accessibility18Safari stays behind; pointer and keyboard untouched
Keys sent to that window2Safari stays behind
Safari in front, briefly2In front for that input only, then your app is in front again

2026-11-12 · Safari 27.2 · macOS 27.2 · a measurement page we built. Covers links and buttons, text fields, menus, dates, scrolling, new tabs and windows, and iframes. The two that come to the front are a menu that opens on pointer-down and a menu revealed by hover.
